card.title: Before I Knew Better
card.instruction: Perform the more hopeful version of yourself from before disappointment taught you caution, and defend that version when reality intrudes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm entering the talent show. At seventeen I invited everyone before I'd even chosen a song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you lost and wouldn't sing for a year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm borrowing the version before that. Will you come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Shall we sit at the back so you can slip out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Front row, please. Seventeen-year-old me expected to spot her friends from the stage.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 adopts the seventeen-year-old invitation habit, A3 explicitly borrows the self before disappointment, and A5 requests visible friends instead of a protected escape.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's year of silence makes A3 define which former self is being borrowed; B4's back-row safety plan causes A5's front-row request.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers the painful loss and B4 offers protective attendance rather than refusing support.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's proposed escape seating to choose the supportive visibility the earlier hopeful self expected.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes entering a talent show and B2 the previous loss that taught caution.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's spot-her-friends ending turns B4's seating choice into a specific defense of hope.
